newsitem.title: INDIA: India CRISIL downgrades Mukerian Papers to BB.
newsitem.headline: India CRISIL downgrades Mukerian Papers to BB.

text.p: India's Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd (CRISIL) said on Wednesday that the rating assigned to the Partly Convertible Debenture Issue of Mukerian Papers Limited (MPL) has been downgraded from "BBB+" to "BB".
The revised rating indicates inadequate safety of timely payment of interest and principal.

While these debentures are less susceptible to default than other speculative grade debentures in the immediate future, the uncertainties that the issuer faces could lead to inadequate capacity to make timely interest and principal payments.

MPL is an agro-based paper manufacturing company operating in the price sensitive, low value segments of the cultural paper market. The company has three paper manufacturing machines with an aggregate capacity of 100 tpd, with its manufacturing facilities located at Mukerian, Punjab.

A recessionary trend seen in the paper industry during the last year has resulted in sharp drop in profitability of MPL for 1996/97. Its future cash flow position is expected to come under strain due to the non conversion of the detachable warrants attached to the PCD issue.

As a result, the debentures still outstanding amounting to around 188 million rupees would now have to be repaid over the period 1998/99 to 2001/02. The interest on the above amount would also become payable from October, 1997 onwards.
